relationship: Constructing a topology and sending a packet connects physical links to connectivity and packet journey outcomes.

learnerLoop.action: Move nodes, add or remove cables, check the topology and send a packet.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The network graph and selectable packet path change.
learnerLoop.evidence: The canvas, feedback and journey text show whether the topology and transfer work.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Rewire the graph or choose another source and destination.

invariants: Topology checks and packet journeys use the current set of nodes and links.
Each visible cable represents a connection in the graph.
safeAdaptations: Change topology challenges, node labels or prompts while retaining editable graph construction and packet testing.
nonGoals: Providing a production network simulator or configuration tool.

task.description: Construct the selected Bus, Star, Mesh or Hybrid network.
task.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

model.description: Placed parts, selected cables and travelling packet routes.
model.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

construction.description: Distinct left parts shelf with the same device artwork in palette, preview and placed item; Move/Cable/Delete and Undo/Reset/Check sit above the bounded canvas.
construction.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

evidence.description: Topology validation and packet testing below the construction canvas; test controls appear after a valid construction.
evidence.visibility: Packet controls appear after a valid construction.

parts.description: Placed network parts and their connectivity.
parts.domain: Task-specific limits on stations, bus cables, switches and bridges.
parts.output: Part counts, model and construction checks.

route.domain: Reachable graph path under the current topology.

modes.tasks: Bus and star require at least four stations; mesh checks direct pairwise links; Hybrid allows mixed existing structures and optional mesh layer.
modes.tools: Move, Cable and Delete; reset and undo alter the graph.

dependencies: Task-specific counts and connection rules must pass before the packet test is shown.
Changing the network invalidates the prior validation.
Routing uses the constructed graph rather than a canned decorative path.
implementation.completion: Check topology records a valid task and enables packet testing; it can be edited and checked again.
limitations: Simplified forwarding and part limits; not physical network provisioning.
Node IDs and palette cards are generated.
